name: Winklern
kurzbeschreibung: Village in the Mölltal valley on the border with Kärnten, offering views of the Großglockner and a lakeside resort.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The market town of Winklern is situated at 966 metres above sea level in the upper Möll Valley, right at the distinctive bend where the valley meets the foot of the historic Iselsberg Pass. Closely connected to East Tyrol and the district capital of Lienz, Winklern serves as an essential alpine crossroads between Carinthia, East Tyrol, and Salzburg. Home to around 1,200 residents, the municipality forms the south-eastern gateway to the High Tauern National Park. Nestled between the glaciated Glockner Group to the north and the rugged Schober Group to the west, Winklern enjoys sweeping views of the Großglockner massif and the dramatic peaks of the Lienz Dolomites.

Geschichte

Ancient pack-mule tracks across the Iselsberg linked the Drau Valley with high-alpine gold mining districts since Roman times. The district of Penzelberg was documented as early as 991–1021, while Winklern itself was first recorded between 1041 and 1060, named after its sheltered position in the corner of the Möll Valley bend. The landmark of the town, the historic Mautturm (Toll Tower), was built around 1300 by the Counts of Görz-Tyrol as a fortified tower to levy duties on precious gold and trade goods crossing the pass. In 1460 it passed into Habsburg ownership. The late-Gothic parish church of St. Lawrence, consecrated in 1521 following a fire, features intricate net-ribbed vaulting and historic 16th-century frescoes.

Anreise

Winklern enjoys convenient road access from several directions. From East Tyrol, the Großglocknerstraße B107 winds from Lienz across the 1,209-metre Iselsberg Pass over a scenic 15-kilometre route into town. Coming from the east, the Mölltalstraße B106 connects from Spittal an der Drau. In summer, the famous Grossglockner High Alpine Road provides an unforgettable mountain route from Salzburg via Heiligenblut. By train, travellers head to Lienz in East Tyrol or Spittal-Millstätter See; from Lienz railway station, regional bus line 5108 runs several times daily across the Iselsberg Pass directly into Winklern.

Tipps

The historic Mautturm now houses an engaging cultural centre showcasing exhibitions on Tauern gold mining and minerals, featuring a panoramic viewing platform overlooking the valley. Outdoor enthusiasts can embark on scenic hikes into the Schober Group, such as ascending to the welcoming Winklerner Hütte at 1,907 metres or conquering the Straßkopf at 2,401 metres for breathtaking vistas of the Großglockner. On warm summer days, the Winklern leisure centre offers a solar-heated adventure pool with water slides and sunbathing lawns. The town is also a perfect entry point for cycling along the Möll Valley on the Glockner Cycle Path R8.
